author: goldturtle
body:
@marcfeuermann @pgaudet: submitted with the PAINT issue template's fields. The posting account cannot set labels, so please add `PAINT annotation`.

* **PTHR ID & PTN node:** PTHR11848; PTN002626375 (gain of positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation, GO:0045669)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** UniProtKB:P55107 GDF10 (growth differentiation factor 10)

* **Type of Issue:** Other: the rat source experiment and GDF10's own experiment conflict.

*How this draft was made:* an automated screen compared every PAN-GO (IBA) annotation of human genes (release 2025-10-12_2.0.5, PANTHER 19) with the genes' experimental annotations in GO release 2025-10-10. Flagged annotations were then judged by evidence-cited reasoning (Claude subagents, citing only a curated evidence pack). The statements below were checked against the GO, PAN-GO and PANTHER data, and the papers behind the key annotations were read. Please treat it as a candidate for curator review.


**Related tracker issue:** [geneontology/go-annotation#4186](https://github.com/geneontology/go-annotation/issues/4186) (2022): BMP-signalling annotations in this family were blocked for some fly genes, and the PAN-GO curators planned to propagate less specific terms in these signalling families.

**Inherited:** GDF10 `involved_in` *positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation* ([GO:0045669](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0045669))

- **Gain:** PTN002626375 (speciation, Euteleostomi; human genes below: GDF10), dated 2023-05-11.
- **Evidence genes (1):** Gdf10 (RAT).
- **Relation to GDF10:** orthologs: Gdf10 (RAT).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** none.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** not annotated.

**GDF10's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation*: 1 opposing, 0 supporting:

- *negative regulation of ossification* ([GO:0030279](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0030279)): [PMID:22155034](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22155034/) (IDA)

**Literature (Textpresso, all species corpora):** 9 sentences mention GDF10 together with *osteoblast differentiation*. By cue words, 5 describe the opposite of the inherited direction and 0 agree.

> BMP-3b, also known as growth differentiation factor 10 (GDF10), is a divergent member of the TGF-β superfamily that is closely related to BMP3 (16) and signals through TGF-β receptors (17, 18, 19). **GDF10 expression correlates with osteoblast differentiation (20) and like BMP3, can inhibit this process (21).** Supporting its role in osteogenic transdifferentiation, single-cell RNAseq of cells derived from the atherosclerotic aorta of Apolipoprotein E-deficient (Apoe−/−) mice revealed that GDF10 is involved in the ossification and osteoblast differentiation of VSMCs (22).

— Platko K, Gyulay G, Lebeau PF, MacDonald ME, Lynn EG, Byun JH et al. (2024). GDF10 is a negative regulator of vascular calcification. *The Journal of biological chemistry*. [PMID:39307303](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39307303/).


> Evidence also suggests that there exists an inverse relationship whereby RUNX2 can regulate GDF10 expression in lung carcinoma and mesenchymal stem cells (36). **Furthermore, GDF10 blocks osteoblast differentiation by attenuating the expression of RUNX2, OCN, and Collagen 1 (21).** These findings provide an additional mechanism to explain the protective phenotype observed in TDAG51−/− mice (34) In the present study, we provide direct evidence that rhGDF10 treatment inhibits Pi-mediate HA mineral deposition in cultured mice and human VSMCs, as well as ex vivo aortic ring cultures.

— Platko K, Gyulay G, Lebeau PF, MacDonald ME, Lynn EG, Byun JH et al. (2024). GDF10 is a negative regulator of vascular calcification. *The Journal of biological chemistry*. [PMID:39307303](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39307303/).


**Sentences counted as agreeing** (0): none.

**Reasoning** (evidence-cited; verdict *error likely*, high confidence; cause: ortholog annotation conflict): The pack consistently shows GDF10 (BMP-3b) inhibiting osteoblast differentiation: an IDA study shows it suppresses osteoblast markers and BMP-induced signaling, and Bmp3b knockout mice have high bone mass with elevated osteoblast gene expression. The inherited positive-regulation term comes from a single rat ortholog annotation and is new in this release. The rat annotation likely reflects GDF10 expression correlating with osteoblast differentiation rather than promoting it.

- *Against:* GDF10 has an IDA annotation to negative regulation of ossification from a study showing BMP-3b suppresses Runx2, osteocalcin and type-1 collagen expression induced by BMP-2/4/6/7. ([PMID:22155034](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22155034/); Matsumoto et al. 2012)
- *Against:* Bmp3b deletion in mice increases bone volume and mineral density and raises osteoblast-differentiation gene expression, and its inactivation enhances osteogenesis of bone marrow stem cells. (Kodama et al. 2025)
- *Against:* Multiple independent sentences describe GDF10 as an established inhibitor of osteoblast differentiation that antagonises BMP-2/4-mediated osteogenesis, and GDF10 also inhibits vascular calcification. (Platko et al. 2024; Ogawa et al. 2018; Platko et al. 2019)
- *For:* The inherited term rests on a single evidence gene, the rat Gdf10 ortholog, met at a speciation node. (Gdf10; PANTHER tree)
- *Context:* GDF10 expression correlates with osteoblast differentiation, which could explain a positive annotation in another species without showing that GDF10 promotes it. (Platko et al. 2024)
- *Context:* The annotation is new: GDF10 did not have it in PAN-GO v1, and the gain was curated in 2023. (PAN-GO v1; PAN-GO annotation)

*Reasoner's suggested fix:* Remove the gain of positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation at PTN002626375, re-review the rat Gdf10 experimental annotation, and consider negative regulation of osteoblast differentiation instead.

*Note on the reasoning:* The pack did not contain the rat source annotation, and the summary's last sentence (that it reflects expression rather than function) is wrong: it comes from an overexpression experiment (see the suggested change). The 'multiple independent sentences' all cite the same study (Matsumoto et al. 2012, [PMID:22155034](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22155034/)).

**Suggested change:**

- *positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation* rests on Gdf10 (RAT), orthologs whose annotations conflict with GDF10's own experimental annotations and the literature. Review those source annotations, or whether this term should propagate, rather than adding a loss.
- The rat source annotation is an IDA from Kaihara et al. 2003 ([PMID:12559390](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12559390/)): adenoviral overexpression of BMP-3b enhanced BMP-2-induced osteoblastic differentiation of C2C12 cells and BMP-2-induced bone formation in rats. GDF10's opposing IDA (Matsumoto et al. 2012, [PMID:22155034](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22155034/)) used the same C2C12 and BMP-2 system with BMP-3b protein and found suppression. In knockout mice, a 1999 study found no obvious abnormalities in the tissues examined ([PMID:10419686](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10419686/)), while a 2025 study reports high bone mass (Kodama et al. 2025), which favours inhibition. This is a conflict between experiments rather than a clear annotation error.

### References
- Kaihara S, Bessho K, Okubo Y, Sonobe J, Komatsu Y, Miura M et al. (2003). Over expression of bone morphogenetic protein-3b (BMP-3b) using an adenoviral vector promote the osteoblastic differentiation in C2C12 cells and augment the bone formation induced by bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) in rats. *Life Sci*. [PMID:12559390](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12559390/).
- Kodama N, Matsubara T, Yoshimura A, Nagano K, Hino J, Tsuji K et al. (2025). BMP3b regulates bone mass by inhibiting BMP signaling. *Bone*. [PMID:39461491](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39461491/).
- Matsumoto Y, Otsuka F, Hino J, Miyoshi T, Takano M, Miyazato M et al. (2012). Bone morphogenetic protein-3b (BMP-3b) inhibits osteoblast differentiation via Smad2/3 pathway by counteracting Smad1/5/8 signaling. *Mol Cell Endocrinol*. [PMID:22155034](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22155034/).
- Ogawa Y, Tsuji M, Tanaka E, Miyazato M, Hino J (2018). Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP)-3b Gene Depletion Causes High Mortality in a Mouse Model of Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy. *Frontiers in neurology*. [PMID:29922215](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29922215/).
- Platko K, Gyulay G, Lebeau PF, MacDonald ME, Lynn EG, Byun JH et al. (2024). GDF10 is a negative regulator of vascular calcification. *The Journal of biological chemistry*. [PMID:39307303](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39307303/).
- Platko K, Lebeau PF, Byun JH, Poon SV, Day EA, MacDonald ME et al. (2019). GDF10 blocks hepatic PPARγ activation to protect against diet-induced liver injury. *Molecular metabolism*. [PMID:31288993](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31288993/).
title: PAINT issue: PTHR11848: GDF10 inherits "positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation", contrary to its own experimental annotations
